failure_summary.description: Answers added supplied role, institution, title, or place words, or used a different inflected form than the expected concise answer.
Returned a school description instead of the person explicitly requested by the clue.
Followed a retrieved idiom definition instead of expanding a name explicitly cued by “stands for.”

patch.reasoning: Most failures are already covered by the skill’s answer-slot and granularity rules, so repeating those instructions would not address a new gap. Add a focused rule for explicit expansion cues, which can prevent a nearby idiom definition from overriding the clue’s request.

edits.target: - In trivia or wordplay clues, treat a parenthetical number as a hard answer-length constraint. For a double-definition clue (for example, “X, or what Y is put to”), seek the exact word that fits both senses rather than a synonym that fits only one. Use any proper-name cue to identify the requested name or name part.
edits.content: - When a clue asks what a name, initialism, or abbreviation “stands for,” give its established expansion. Do not let a nearby idiom or dictionary definition override that explicit cue; resolve the whole clue before choosing which sense is requested.
